newsitem.title: USA: Canada hopes for spring IMF pacts on SDRs, quotas.
newsitem.headline: Canada hopes for spring IMF pacts on SDRs, quotas.

text.p: Canada is hoping for agreements in the spring on proposals for the IMF to issue more of its artificial currency and increase its capital base, a senior Canadian official said on Saturday.

International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus has called for a selective issue of 26 billion Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) and a doubling of the IMF's 145 billion SDRs in capital through a so-called quota increase.
The SDR is currently worth about $1.44.
The SDR issue would be an "equity" allocation mainly aimed at the more than 35 countries that have joined the IMF since the artificial currency was last handed out in 1981.
The Group of Seven -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- has proposed a 16 billion SDR equity allocation.
"The final answer will be somewhere between 16 and 26 billion," the Canadian official said. "By the time of the spring meeting the details of the numbers should be worked out," he added.
Canada would also like an agreement at the spring meeting on a plan to increase the IMF's capital.

"Once again it will be a question of what is the appropriate size of the increase," the senior Canadian official said, adding, "There have been a range of numbers put on the table, from 50 percent to a doubling."
